ModMetaData.name: Variety Matters Redux
ModMetaData.author: Evyatar108
ModMetaData.description:
Pawns get tired of eating the same thing. Every colonist has a Food Variety need that looks at the ingredients in their recent meals. A meal made from ingredients they haven't had lately counts as fresh, and a meal that repeats the last few dinners counts for little. The need drives a mood thought with 13 steps, from a barren menu at -12 to an overwhelming one at +12 by default.
Cooks do their part. When a bill allows mixed ingredients, the cook reaches for ingredients they haven't used lately, so meals rotate through your freezer instead of the same three berries every time. Pawns choosing a meal lean toward the one that does their variety the most good.
Wealthy and titled pawns expect more variety. Gourmands care twice as much, ascetics don't care at all, and with Biotech the "no taste" gene turns the need off; sanguophages have it by default. Pawns also settle on favourite foods, one meat and one vegetable (Gourmands get a third pick), and get a small mood boost when they eat one.
Hover over the need for a pawn's recent meals, or open its details window to see why each meal scored as it did. The settings offer Easy, Default and Hardcore presets, and you can change every number.
